title: Double Dragon
build: Two Mastertronic G64 disk variants, with disk IDs AD and TO

records.c: The 6510 port direction register. The game changes the memory mapping through the output register at $0001.
The 6510 port output register. $2D33 selects the mapping for the raster interrupt. $63D5 changes the setting in the ending path.
Fixed offsets 0, 7 and 14 select the SID register group for each of the three voices.
Early signed pitch entries read through the instrument profile pointer. The pointer at $0D0D selects $03AA for its pitch data.
A separator at $03B3 before the two arrays of stream pointers at $03B4–$03B9. The initializer fills them from the selected sound record.
Low bytes of the three voice order-stream pointers. Sound initialization at $042C fills them, and the order interpreter can replace them for a restart.
High bytes of the three voice order-stream pointers. $04B8 reads the high byte of the current voice's pointer.
First of the three per-voice age counters. The update at $04A0 increments it, and the new pattern at $0548 clears it.
Second per-voice age counter, initialized by $045E.
Third per-voice age counter, initialized by $0461.
Three effect pointer low bytes filled from $0D6E at $05DA. The instrument path reads the current voice's low byte at $06F6.
High bytes of three pointers used by the pitch effect. The driver writes them at $05E0 and reads them to patch the indexed pitch fetches.
Start of the gate and waveform strip selected by the pointer at $0D0B. The update at $0A88 copies a byte to the channel's control state.
Another waveform sequence selected by the pointer at $0CFF. Its first byte gives the age limit installed at $0A84.
Pitch values selected alongside the waveform sequence at $03CE. The update reads them through the operand at $0A9C.
Waveform sequence selected by $0D03, with a longer initial age limit and repeated $14 control values.
The byte before the two short order streams. It is $4C at the AD cold hand-over and $84 in the TO mission snapshot. The interpreter starts these streams at $0409 and $040C.
Bytes before the short sound order streams at $0409 and $040C. The final six bytes form JMP stubs targeting $048F and $04FD.
Second stream from selector 11's entry at $0C62. The driver reads this sequence at $04C9.
First stream from selector 11's entry at $0C62. The driver reads this sequence at $04C9.

Uses X as a sound selector. Copies six bytes of stream pointers from $0C20 into $03B4-$03B9 and the mode byte from $0C14 into $0495. Clears the voice state and writes the initial volume and envelope registers.
Saved selector added back while calculating the six-byte offset in the order pointer table. The next loop copies the three low and three high bytes.
Current sound selector stored in the immediate operand of the LDA at $043B. The order reader also checks this byte to decide whether to use the title tune's restart pointers.
Low address byte of the store to the third voice's attack and decay register at $047E.
High address byte of the store to the third voice's sustain and release register at $0481.
Sets the update guard at $048E, then clears control and envelope registers for the three voices through $0467.
Returns while the guard at $048E is nonzero. Otherwise it traverses three SID voices using the stream pointers at $03B4 and $03B7.
Operand of the LDA at $048D. Zero branches into the update at $0492; any other value returns.
Setup writes the selected cue's mode into this immediate byte. The update loop then initializes the visit to the voices, sets the register offset and reads the current order.
Reads the next command at the current voice's stream address. $FE halts the driver. $FF resets its counters and, on selection 0, installs replacement stream pointers from $0C68 and $0C6B.
Low operand of the indexed read at $04C9, patched with the current voice's order-stream pointer.
Patched high byte of the order read at $04C9. The interpreter tests incoming bytes for end or restart, then separates pitch, speed and pattern selections by their ranges.
Three bytes decode as LDA $0390. The preceding order-command path jumps back before it, and the pattern lookup starts at $0534.
Doubles the order value and reads a little-endian pattern pointer at $0C6E. Handles leading filter commands and commands that set voice parameters before the note.
Copies the duration to the countdown, adds the voice's transposition to the note index, fetches its two frequency bytes from $0B5E and $0BB9, then writes the frequency and envelope for that voice.
Advances the voice pattern index past the filter setting. Stores the next pattern byte for further decoding unless it is the end command.
Uses eight-byte instrument records. Loads the last three fields into $E1–$E3 and tests the flags to select later waveform and pitch calculations.
High byte of the STA at $0702. This store patches the high address byte of the restart fetch at $070D.
Low operand of the restart fetch at $070D, patched from the selected effect pointer.
High operand of the fetch at $070D. When the effect index underflows, that read resets the current voice's index before the next pitch lookup.
Low operand of the indexed read at $0719. The pitch update combines that fetched effect entry with the note index.
Patched high byte of the indexed read at $0719. The loaded byte is added to the note index before fetching its frequency word.
The code rewrites the first opcode here from the high bit of $E1. Changes whether this pass adds or subtracts the note-spacing term before writing the pitch.
Instrument-specific limit patched into the CMP at $07C8. The note age controls whether the loop subtracts another pitch increment.
Immediate operand read after pulling the shifted note-step calculation. The path measures the distance between the current note and its stored target using both pitch tables.
Part of the slide calculation that adds each fractional step, shifts its two-byte result and patches the later pitch update.
The store at $0873 replaces this CLC or SEC with the chosen carry instruction before the two-byte pitch addition.
Patched ADC or SBC opcode for the low frequency. The result is saved before the operation on the high byte.
Low byte of the pitch increment, patched by $08AD before the two-byte slide operation.
Patched ADC or SBC opcode for the high frequency, using the carry from the low-byte operation.
The immediate of the ADC at $08C5. The path writes the adjusted high frequency, or reloads the note target and clears slide state, then checks the voice's instrument for further changes.
In the selector 6 trace, the voice reads this profile to set the filter mode and select a cutoff change by the voice's age.
Advances into later age boundaries in the waveform table. Branches select a signed step and update the voice's current stage according to its age.
Patched high-byte ceiling compared after stepping the pulse. The next path increments or decrements the two-byte state and checks another profile bound.
Immediate limit in the comparison at $0996. The boundary selects whether the current age can still be used for the indexed waveform path.
Immediate gate setting read on the timed waveform path. The surrounding code uses the selected profile to keep or reset waveform state and sets up the optional filter path.
Operand of the LDA at $09DA. $09DC installs it as the low byte of the filter profile pointer in $E5.
Low part of the indirect filter profile address. The path reads the mode and decides which cutoff entry to use by comparing the voice age with profile boundaries.
Starts with bytes read indirectly by $0551 and its continuation in the selector 1 test. These are pattern data addressed by the pointer table, despite residing amid the driver routines.
Converts a selected time entry to its delta position in the filter profile. Adds the delta to that voice's stored cutoff and routes the result to the cutoff register.
Low operand of the waveform-length fetch at $0A78. The selected voice profile supplies the address.
High operand of the waveform-length fetch at $0A78. The returned first byte becomes the current waveform's age limit.
Age limit in the operand of CMP at $0A83. The update skips the remaining waveform steps when the voice's age is at least this value.
Low operand of the indexed fetch at $0A88. Patched from the selected waveform profile.
High byte of the load at $0A88. The loaded control value sets the voice's waveform and contributes to the following gate mask.
Low byte of the indexed pitch fetch at $0A9C, patched from the pitch pointer for the selected voice profile.
High byte of the pitch-profile fetch at $0A9C. The effect uses the byte as either a relative note adjustment or part of an absolute pitch write.
Pattern bytes read by the three-voice title/ending selection. $0551 reads its first token and its continuation at $06A7 or $0663 reads later values.
In this profile path uses the profile byte as the high frequency and sets the low frequency to zero, then writes the voice registers via $0B24.
Patched operand used before restoring the stored pitch and waveform for a voice. The continuation masks its control byte and writes it to the active SID channel.
Low bytes of the SID frequency values, indexed by note after adding the voice transposition.
The same low-byte frequency table seen from its second byte. The note-spacing routine subtracts the current note's low byte from this next note.
Tail of the low-byte frequency table, indices $41 through $5A. The next voice pitch fetch uses the same index for the corresponding high byte.
High bytes paired with $0B5E. A change of pitch can read both tables again without starting a fresh note.
The next note's high byte for the same subtraction after the low bytes have set carry.
Tail of the matching high-frequency byte table, also indexed from $41 through $5A.
Twelve mode bytes indexed by X in the sound initializer; $0419 writes the selected mode into the immediate operand at $0495.
Selector 0: the three stream addresses are $0F00, $0FA8, $0FEC. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Selector 1: the three stream addresses are $13C3, $13C6, $13D2. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Selector 2: the three stream addresses are $148B, $148D, $1517. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Selector 3: the three stream addresses are $149C, $149F, $1517. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Selector 4: the three stream addresses are $14A7, $1517, $1517. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Selector 5: the three stream addresses are $14AF, $1517, $1517. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Selector 6: the three stream addresses are $14BA, $1517, $1517. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Selector 7: the three stream addresses are $14C5, $14C7, $1517. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Selector 8: the three stream addresses are $14EF, $1517, $1517. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Selector 9: the three stream addresses are $14F7, $1517, $1517. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Selector 10: the three stream addresses are $1502, $1517, $1517. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Selector 11: the three stream addresses are $040C, $0409, $1517. The initializer loads three low bytes followed by three high bytes.
Three low bytes used when selector 0 reaches its $FF order command and restarts the voices.
The matching three high bytes used with the low bytes at $0C68.
Two bytes per pattern starting at this address. $0534 doubles the pattern number and reads its pointer; later pattern numbers select the entries in the $0CAF area.
High bytes of the pattern pointers at $0C6E. The lookup at $053B uses twice the pattern number as its index.
High byte of the entry at $0CAE, which points to $13DB. More pattern pointers and short order data share this region before the voice profile at $0CF3.
Four bytes per voice profile, made of two little-endian pointers. The first addresses the waveform strip and the second the pitch adjustments.
High byte of the first profile's waveform pointer. $0A63 reads this field for the selected profile.
Low byte of the first profile's pitch adjustment pointer. $0A6C reads it for the selected profile.
High byte of the first profile's pitch pointer. The update at $0A72 reads this field with the other three bytes, then patches its effect program reads.
Default waveform and gate values in the first profile in the pointer table. Its first value is also the age limit.
The default strip of pitch adjustments selected by the first record at $0CF3. The update uses it when the relevant instrument flag is set.
Indirect data sampled for selector 0 through the note calculation entry at $0A9F, which adds the byte to the current note when the instrument flag selects that path.
Low bytes of twelve pointers read at $05D5. The selected pointer heads an effect sequence used by the voice update.
High bytes paired with $0D6E, read at $05DD using the same index.
$09CE takes a low pointer byte here and patches the LDA at $09DA before redirecting the filter profile lookup.
Values below the main instrument records. $09AF uses an instrument bit test to branch into the filter setup and its parameter lookup.
The routine at $08FF reads the selected profile's flags and timing entries here. It patches thresholds and chooses an entry by the current note age.
Records of eight bytes. The third and fourth bytes become the attack/decay and sustain/release values. $06CB uses the last three as waveform and effect parameters.
$0634 reads this per-instrument field into $034A and $0372 for the current voice.
Attack and decay in each eight-byte instrument record. $0620 reads this field and writes it to the selected voice's SID register.
Sustain and release in each eight-byte instrument record, copied to the active SID voice at $0629.
$062C reads this field at the eight-byte record stride and pushes it for the rest of the voice setup.
$06D2 reads this field at the eight-byte record stride into $E1 for the pitch effect calculations.
$06D7 reads this field at the eight-byte record stride into $E2.
The flags field of the first eight-byte SID instrument record. The lookup at $06E2 uses eight times the voice's instrument number to read the corresponding field.
Flags byte for instrument 9, at offset $48 from $0DE3. More records follow at an eight-byte stride.
Flags byte for instrument 17, at offset $80 from $0DE3. This group continues to the separate instrument-indexed table at $0EC4.
Bytes at this end of the instrument-record area. The envelope and waveform tables share the same eight-byte stride from their base addresses in the first record.
Twenty per-instrument bytes. The pitch update reads this value when patching the note age comparison at $07C8.
Twenty instrument-indexed bytes beside the age limit table. The sound effect code looks up corresponding entries by the same instrument number.
Later twenty-byte instrument table. The driver reads its values separately from the corresponding parameter set at $0ED8.
First title/ending voice starts here. The order interpreter at $04C9 reads these bytes through its patched load operand and uses small values to index the pattern addresses.
One restart order stream for title selection 0. The low and high bytes at $0C68 and $0C6B give this address to the first voice.
Continuation of the order stream beginning at $0F13. The order reader advances the offset in $0347; a low order byte is used as a pattern number.
Last portion of the order stream region before the second voice starts at $0FAD.
The order stream for the second voice of selector 0. The driver loads this address from the first record at $0C20.
The order stream for the third voice of selector 0. It supplies pattern selections as the other two streams advance independently.

Part of the title and ending's stored pattern area. The music reader uses the table at $0C6E to select shorter pieces within it; the name at the start also appears as a placeholder for patched reads elsewhere.
Data in the following area is read through the pattern pointer. The selector 0 and 11 traces together reach 240 distinct bytes of the $1040–$1398 span in 1,600 calls each.
A pitch-effect sequence used through the two patched operands at $070D and $0719. After reading the count, the code reads following bytes and adds them to the base pitch index.
First order pointer for selection 1. The corresponding pointers for its other two voices are $13C6 and $13D2.
Starts a region the second selection reads through the shared pattern decoder, including the filter write path through $055F.
Last byte read in the selector 1 trace. Effects use more data after this address and can share the same pattern reader.
First two orders for selector 2 start at $148B and $148D. The third voice uses the common $1517 pointer.
First two orders for selector 3 start at $149C and $149F.
First voice's order data for selector 4. Both remaining voices point at $1517.
First voice's order data for selector 5. The two remaining voice entries share $1517.
First voice's order data for selector 6. Its trace also reads the filter profile at $0936.
First voice order for selector 7. The second starts two bytes later at $14C7.
First voice's order for selector 8. The latest byte read in its bounded run is $14F6.
First voice's order for selector 9. The other two voice entries both use $1517.
First voice's order for selector 10. Voices two and three have the same $1517 start address.
Shared order pointer in most of the effect rows. Points to one byte, separate from the active voice's stream.
Jumps to the new-game setup at $2C11. The following bytes starting at $2C03 are mutable gameplay state.
An index below $80 requests a new SID selection. The update routine at $2E8D consumes it and replaces it with $80.
Current level resource index. Setup at $2C11 begins at zero. The transition at $63B7 uses 0 through 5 as the disk selector and sends 6 to the ending path.
Character identity used in the first player's support scan. The loop advances it in $3A55 and compares it with the candidate characters.
Character identity used in the second player's counterpart scan. $3AB9 advances it during that scan.
First actor state checked before writing the next movement step. The support scan increments it at $3A1F.
Second actor counterpart, incremented at $3A83 and read at $2E20 before updating that player.
Short movement counter incremented at $33F8, read back immediately for the periodic update.
Resets the resource index, takes the title's selection from $1A63 minus one into $2F0A, calls common score and life setup, then falls through to level setup.

Resets the level's gameplay state, copies the initial actor sprite pointers, sets up video and the level initialisation calls, then installs the hardware IRQ at $2D5E and enters the main loop at $5FE5. The disk transition at $63C2 enters here without resetting the resource index.
Saves A, Y and X and acknowledges the VIC interrupt. Dispatches the four states 0 to 3 from zero-page $34 to $308E, $319C, $3252 or $32C0; other values take the longer update starting at $2D8F.
An $EA byte between the jump to the top-of-frame update and the first lower-body jump stub.
The first raster-change case jumps to $308E, which writes the lower-half sprite positions and pointers. The next three jump stubs handle the other positions in sorted order.

Updates scrolling and sprite setup, advances player recovery or action states, and polls a port when its actor is ready. The active-player mode gates each actor's calls. The routine then checks the camera constraints, player contact and pending sound.
When $2C04 is nonnegative, starts that sound through $040E and then writes $80 to mark the request handled. On the negative path calls the regular SID update at $048D instead.
Four vertical positions. The drawing order compares these at $2F22, and the first set of sprite layers uses them as the VIC Y coordinates.
Four actor indices sorted by vertical position at $2F11. Adjacent entries with equal Y keep their order.
Second actor number in the raster sort order. The first group switch reads it at $3019.
Third actor number in raster sort order. The next setup reads it at $302F.
Fourth actor number in raster sort order. The final group setup reads it at $3045.
Four bytes per actor in sixteen bytes. The first two give the overlaid shapes above the waist and the second two give the shapes below it.
VIC sprite pointer for player 1’s upper colour layer. The pose handlers update it before the raster sprite setup reads it.
VIC sprite pointer for player 1’s lower outline layer. The pose handlers update it before the raster sprite setup reads it.
VIC sprite pointer for player 1’s lower colour layer. The pose handlers update it before the raster sprite setup reads it.
VIC sprite pointer for player 2’s upper outline layer. The pose handlers update it before the raster sprite setup reads it.
VIC sprite pointer for player 2’s upper colour layer. The pose handlers update it before the raster sprite setup reads it.
VIC sprite pointer for player 2’s lower outline layer. The pose handlers update it before the raster sprite setup reads it.
VIC sprite pointer for player 2’s lower colour layer. The pose handlers update it before the raster sprite setup reads it.
Four VIC pointer numbers for the first enemy, written by the shape selector. A pose writes upper outline and colour first, then lower outline and colour.
Four shape pointers for the second enemy. $6AA6 and the other direction branches fill them from the active pose script.
Low eight bits of four actor X positions. Port 2's right branch increments the first actor's value twice, subject to movement checks.
Starting upper-half sprite colour for the actor indexed in $2FC8. That sprite setup reads a neighbouring value for the lower half.
The lower-half colour paired with the first actor's upper colour. The indexed reads use the actor's doubled colour offset.
Loaded from the enemy type's upper colour at $6733.
Loaded from the enemy type's lower colour at $6739.
Loaded from the second enemy type's upper colour at $6A59.
Loaded from the second enemy type's lower colour at $6A5F.
The movement handlers advance this byte and select new shapes as the phase changes.
The second fighter's movement animation phase. Its branches update it at $411B and the corresponding direction entries.
Zero after moving left through $350A, one after moving right through $35A4. The fire dispatcher reads this to choose between two direction dispatches.
The second player’s facing used by the dispatch. Horizontal movement stores the direction here.
The first player's directional movement handlers overwrite this byte as the candidate movement changes.
The second player's directional movement handlers overwrite this byte in their equivalent branches.
Attack or movement state for the first actor. $4417 doubles it to select a routine from the little-endian jump table starting at $442B.
The action handlers advance this byte to select the next part of an attack or jump, after fire dispatch clears it.
Starting coordinate used in the first fighter's jump handler. Fire dispatch stores it before entering an action.
Candidate coordinate stored and tested by the first fighter's jump actions at $4823 and $486F.
Port 1's fire dispatcher stores the second actor's state here. For example, $4B15 stores $01 for left and fire when the second actor faces left.
The second fighter's corresponding action step. The first handler in the jump table advances it at $4C83.
Starting coordinate used in the second fighter's corresponding jump action.
Candidate coordinate stored at $4FF0 and used by the second fighter's jump test near $503C.
The update distinguishes 0 (first player only), 1 (both players) and 2 (second player only). The first or second player leaving play can change mode 1 to 2 or 0 respectively.
Sorts four actor indices by nondecreasing Y, then copies each actor's four sprite pointers into $24–$33 and two colour values into $35–$3C in that order.

Schedules each upper-to-lower sprite change at actor Y plus 19, capped at $D5. Holds the new sprite Y two lines below that scheduled time. Later comparisons adjust the schedule when changes are close together.

Places four sprite pairs at the sorted actor coordinates. Each pair uses matching X and Y and writes pointers in both graphics screen buffers. Separate pointer pairs are installed during the raster changes.
Writes a common Y to sprites 0 and 1, a common X from $2EEC,Y, and the pair of shape pointers at $30 and $31 to both screen buffers.
Increments the end wait counter. At count $64 sets the flag to return to the title. Sets both players' low X coordinate to 2 on each pass.
Calls both enemy contact routines while the end flags are clear. Otherwise it counts the delayed exit for the corresponding actor.
If set, the collision sampler takes the proposed X from $344A instead of the actor X.
Flag selecting the second player's proposed X from $344B during a collision query.
Flag selecting the first player's proposed Y at $344C instead of the actor Y. $37F9 consumes it.
Flag selecting the second player's proposed Y from $344D during a collision query.
Candidate first player X written before testing the map.
Candidate second player X written before testing the map.
Candidate first player Y read at $3803.
Candidate second player Y read by the matching query at $3FB6.
Fire dispatch sets it and waits for the movement path to clear it before dispatching again.
Second fighter's equivalent gate. The attack dispatch at $4A38 skips when this is set.

Reads CIA 1 port A for joystick 2. Tests fire before the direction comparisons when $344E is clear; otherwise advances the counter at $421A and clears the gate at $1B. The direction comparisons dispatch the selected direction or diagonal.
Uses either the queued Y probe or the first actor's Y to index a row-pointer table. Chooses a row in the active display buffer and tests the addressed character in the first tile mask set.
The low address byte of the LDA at $384F selects the row read used by the first player’s first map property test. Written at $381C and $382B.
The high address byte of the LDA at $384F selects the row read used by the first player’s first map property test. Written at $3822 and $3831.
Reads a character from the patched first-player row and uses the level and scrolling position to pick the first tile property table.
The low address byte of the LDA at $3873 selects the first player’s selected collision mask table. Written at $386A.
High byte patched by the level and camera position. The lookup uses the tile code's high five bits for the table byte and low three for the bit.
Eight masks, high to low. The collision samplers use the character's bottom three bits to select one bit from its packed property byte.
Low bytes of the pointer pairs selecting the first collision mask set. $3867 reads them using a doubled selector.
High bytes paired with the low bytes at $38A0. The selected pair depends on resource index and, for the first two scenes, the camera column.
Low bytes of the pointer pairs selecting the second collision mask set. $393E reads them using a doubled selector.
High bytes for the second packed property tables. The movement probes use them with the first bytes at $38B8.
Uses the current screen buffer and the second property table for the first player. It patches the row and mask loads to address the correct tile and table.
The low address byte of the LDA at $3926 selects the row read used by the first player’s second map property test. Written at $38F3 and $3902.
High address byte of the patched first-player screen row read in the second property test. The read gives the tile code used for the mask.
The low address byte of the LDA at $394A selects the first player’s selected second collision mask table. Written at $3941.
High byte of the patched address at $394A, which looks up the byte of the first player's second tile property table.
Low bytes of the address pairs for display buffer A. The sampler selects a row with a doubled index.
The high address byte of each row in the first display buffer. The lookup doubles the row number and reads this table and $396F together.
Final three bytes before buffer B's row table. The last two form the same $39F7 fallback address repeated around the tables.
Low bytes of the row pointers for display buffer B. The high bytes start at $39B4.
The high address byte of each row in the second display buffer, paired with the low byte at $39B3.
Starts looking for a return position when the recovery counter reaches $4B. Holds the counter at $4A while the chosen display row is tested.
The low address byte of the LDA at $3A42 selects the screen row used by the first player support-character scan. Written at $3A37.
Final byte of the patched absolute indexed load for the first player's return scan. When it finds a suitable tile, the code computes an X from the column and clears the recovery counter.
Counts the corresponding recovery wait, uses the row state at $2C07 and prepares the second actor's placement scan.
The low address byte of the LDA at $3AA6 selects the screen row used by the second player support-character scan. Written at $3A9B.
High byte of the indexed map fetch at $3AA6, patched from the row pointer table. The scan tests columns 12 through 25 and uses the first eligible tile to compute the second player's X and Y.

Reads CIA 1 port B for joystick 1. Tests fire before the direction comparisons when $344F is clear; otherwise advances the counter at $421B and clears the gate at $1B. The direction comparisons dispatch the selected direction or diagonal.
Takes the second player's Y or the probe override. Translates the position to a tile in the current screen buffer and uses the first mask set.
The low address byte of the LDA at $400C selects the second player’s first collision probe row. Written at $3FD9 and $3FE8.
The high address byte of the LDA at $400C selects the second player’s first collision probe row. Written at $3FDF and $3FEE.
Reads the candidate character from the patched second-player row and selects the first tile property table used for that level.
The low address byte of the LDA at $4030 selects the collision mask selected for the second player’s first probe. Written at $4027.
High byte of the patched address at $4030. The following bit test uses the low three tile bits to choose from the table byte.
Reads the second player's X and Y or the movement overrides. Selects the second per-level tile property table before returning the sampled bit.
The low address byte of the LDA at $40AB selects the second player’s second collision probe row. Written at $4078 and $4087.
High byte of the second player's patched screen-row read. Supplies the character code for the second property table.
The low address byte of the LDA at $40CF selects the collision mask selected for the second player’s second probe. Written at $40C6.

High byte of the table address in the LDA at $40CF. The level and two camera column thresholds select a tile collision mask table. The high five bits of the tile code index it and the low three choose its bit.
Reset on dispatch at $422C and incremented during the first fighter's input update.
Reset on dispatch at $4A45 and incremented during the second fighter's input update.
Stage state reset at $2C25 and written by the stage condition near $5905.
Cleared at $590A and incremented before the conditional stage test at $5919.
Cleared at $590D and incremented before the second stage test at $5928.
Starts the fire gate. On level resource 3 it checks four background tile IDs before dispatching. For eligible positions, it checks the facing byte and one of nine port-2 direction and fire values.
The low address byte of the LDA at $426C selects the row read testing a stage-specific exception to first-player fire input. Written at $4249 and $4258.
Patched high byte of the stage L3 screen read at $426C. The following code refuses the four special tiles $50–$53 before choosing a facing dispatcher.
Clears the attack counter at $2F03 and compares the port with neutral fire or one of eight directions. The handlers select action IDs, with some choices consulting the weapon variable at $2F00.

Compares the same nine port-2 values as the left-facing dispatcher. The branches choose right-facing attack states. Both facings use $12 for up-right and $11 for up-left, and preserve the actor's initial Y for those jumps.
Reads a pointer from the table at $442B and patches the absolute JMP at $4428. The table index is twice the action ID at $2F02.
The low address byte of the JMP at $4428 selects the jump to the selected handler in the first player’s action table. Written at $441F.
